messages:
Raj (sales): Heads-up: CardinalMed POC next week. Netsec insists SNI must be visible to their DMZ inspector and they need original client IPs in app logs for auditing. They also prefer not to open cross-account peering if possible. Need clear options + a one-line 5TB/month cost delta for the SOW.

Elise (solutions): Short answer: there are three practical patterns: 1) VPC peering — preserves src IP and lets their DMZ see SNI if TLS is terminated before peering. 2) PrivateLink — isolates network (no peering) but endpoint ENIs appear as source IPs; you can reconstruct client IPs via X-Forwarded-For if the customer terminates TLS at a proxy. 3) Hybrid GWLB/proxy — more infra on customer side but can provide inspection + preserved identity.

Noah (netops): Quick sketches:
- Peering: OnPrem -> DMZ Inspector -> TGW/spoke -> Peering -> Redwood-Private-VPC (no NAT) => srcIP preserved.
- PrivateLink: OnPrem -> DMZ Inspector -> TGW/spoke -> Interface Endpoint -> Endpoint ENI -> Redwood (src=endpoint ENI).
- Hybrid: DMZ -> inline proxy (terminate/re-TLS) -> TGW -> Peering/Proxy-path -> Redwood (proxy injects XFF).

Noah (netops): Firewall paste (customer ops):
```
# If using PrivateLink (interface endpoint)
Allow TCP/443 -> <interface-endpoint-subnet-cidrs>   # endpoint ENIs
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-controlplane-ips>        # if instructed by onboarding

# If using VPC Peering
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-peering-cidr>

# Common
Enforce TLS >= 1.2; deny legacy ciphers
Log and monitor X-Forwarded-For if terminating/re-TLSing
```

Tara (security): For the security questionnaire and SOW please include KMS/HSM language and the TLS-inspect caveat. Suggested copy: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integration; customer keys are not stored in plaintext and key usage is auditable and exportable. If TLS inspection is performed in-customer, the customer must terminate and re-establish TLS to Redwood (we support mTLS and customer CAs)."

Elise (solutions): Cost delta (very rough) for SOW, single line: PrivateLink infra ~= endpoint hourly (~$0.01/hr) + data processing ~$0.01/GB => ~ $5060/mo for 5TB (excl cloud provider egress); VPC peering: no endpoint/data-processing fee, cross-VPC transfer ~ $0.005B0.02/GB => ~ $25100/mo. Peering often cheaper at scale but needs peering approvals.

Raj (sales): They want a hybrid that avoids peering if possible but still gives SNI + client id. Is GWLB + inline proxy viable?

Noah (netops): Yes, GWLB + customer inline proxy can terminate TLS (DMZ inspector sees SNI), then re-TLS into a path that preserves client identity via headers or peering to our VPC. That path requires customer infra (GWLB, proxy), config to preserve XFF, and extra validation; mark as integration work.

Tara (security): Blockers to call out in SOW: 1) If customer policy forbids any TLS re-termination, cannot both inspect SNI and retain original client IPs. 2) If they refuse to allow endpoint ENI CIDRs through their firewall, PrivateLink onboarding stalls. 3) Air-gapped/regulatory requests may require Private on-prem package and longer lead time.

Elise (solutions): SOW blurb (drop-in): "Recommendation: For CardinalMeds POC we recommend VPC peering when both SNI visibility to an inline DMZ TLS inspector and preservation of original client IPs are required, since peering preserves network source IPs and avoids proxy re-termination. If cross-account peering cannot be approved, PrivateLink is an alternative but requires TLS termination at a customer-side proxy (or insertion of X-Forwarded-For) and incurs modest per-GB interface processing fees; GWLB+proxy can be used as a hybrid to satisfy inspection and identity requirements but adds customer infra and validation work. The engineering handoff will include exact CIDRs, firewall allowlists, and an onboarding checklist."

ticket-bot: Created ticket RW-5120: "CardinalMed POC - SNI vs srcIP topology + cost delta" and attached runbook stub.

Raj (sales): Perfect. Elise/Noah, please upload a 1-page runbook and the exact allowlist lines into the ticket so I can attach to the SOW. I'll follow up with CardinalMed today. :thumbsup:
